messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can users access HMC tuned eps and L from a Stan fit?
parts:
That can be helpful for teaching yourself how HMC works, but
let me caution that Stan is state-of-the-art in tuning and it will
be difficult to do much better. Moreover, the total number of
leapfrog steps is dynamic and varies from iteration to iteration.

fit <- stan.fit(….)

get_sampler_params(fit, inc_warmup=FALSE)[,’stepsize__’]
get_sampler_params(fit, inc_warmup=FALSE)[,’n_leapfrog__' ]

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can users access HMC tuned eps and L from a Stan fit?
parts:
You can do that in PyMC3. But you don't want to use static HMC
--- you ant to use NUTS. Static HMC is very hard to tune.

Combining samplers will be easier in Stan once we allow the
mass matrix and step size to be set manually (maybe six months
to a year out, realistically). Otherwise, you can use the Stan
C++ code, code the discrete parameters as data, and just update
the Stan model's data member variables.

- Bob
